To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we report a 39μm×27μm on-chip thermal sensor that uses the temperature-dependent leakage current of a p-n diode in a lateral CMOS SOI technology to monitor the thermal behavior of a 32 nm microprocessor core.
we report an on-chip temperature measurement circuit that uses a diode as the sensing device.
the proposed sensor achieves a 3σ temperature accuracy of ±1.9°C across a wide temperature range of 5°C- 100°C, while consuming only 110 μW from a 1.65 V single supply.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of on-chip thermal sensors that can monitor the thermal profile within a 32-nanometer microprocessor chip.

the development of novel CMOS-based integrated temperature sensors for the purpose of monitoring the thermal profile in a microprocessor core and for the purpose of thermal control of microelectromechanical systems (MEMS).
the design of an integrated temperature sensor for the measurement of the temperature distribution of the core of a microprocessor.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this work presents a novel on-chip temperature sensing technique which is suitable for a broad range of temperature sensing applications in 32-nanometer and future CMOS technology nodes.
the sensor has demonstrated a 3σ inaccuracy of ±3°C across the 0°C-100°C range, while consuming only 200 μW from a 1.65 V supply.
the temperature sensor presented in this work has been successfully fabricated in 32-nM SOI CMOS and has been shown to be a viable solution to the on-chip temperature sensing challenge.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this sensor is capable of monitoring the thermal profile in a microprocessor core and can be integrated with other circuits in a 32-nM SOI technology node.
we have demonstrated an on-chip temperature sensing technique that is based on the reverse-bias current of a self-discharging lateral diode in a 32-nanometer SOI CMOS process.
we are the first to report an on-chip temperature sensing circuit that can be used to monitor the thermal behavior of a high-performance 32-nm CMOS microprocessor core.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a simple diode can be used for accurate temperature measurement.
by using a simple self-discharging diode, a compact on-chip temperature measurement can be realized with high accuracy and low power consumption.
a lateral SOI CMOS p-n junction diode can be used to measure temperature, which has not been reported in the literature before.
